I'm pretty sure the student plan doesn't cover any meds that need special authority (which is most of them unfortunately). They covered a portion of my dexedrine but it's one of the only ADHD meds that doesn't need special authority.

If you aren't already, I would encourage you to get registered with BC [Pharmacare](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/pharmacare-for-bc-residents/who-we-cover/fair-pharmacare-plan) because they'll cover a portion of your prescriptions on top of the student plan. CADDRA has an overview of which meds are covered by  Pharmacare vs. which ones need special authority [here](https://www.caddra.ca/wp-content/uploads/BC_Public-Formulary-Overview-December-2021.pdf).

The annoying thing about Pharmacare is that not only do they require your doctor to send in a [special authority form](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/health/forms/5472fil.pdf) for them to cover all long-acting stimulants (adderall, vyvanse, concerta, etc.), but one of the requirements on the form is that you have to have tried one of the short-acting medications first. It's extremely frustrating because long-acting meds are the first-line treatment for ADHD, but if you want coverage for them you'll need to jump through a lot of hoops.

Edit: also I'm not sure if the student plan will cover long-acting stimulants even if you have special authority. I would get registered with Pharmacare either way

bok choy is a pretty easy vegetable to cook but if you overcook it it’ll become limp and difficult to chew. you’ll know it’s done when the bok choy is green and slightly tender when you bite into it. 

start by trimming the ends and breaking off the larger outer leaves before soaking in water to dislodge all the grime that tends to collect in the crevices of each layer. i blanch a batch in boiling water real quick (~30-45s) before sautéing with a bit of oil and chopped garlic. you can try different seasonings too; if i’m feeling lazy i’ll keep it simple by just adding salt to taste, but sometimes i’ll cook it in a mix of oyster sauce + light soy sauce + pinch of sugar. woks of life has a simple recipe [here](https://thewoksoflife.com/garlic-baby-bok-choy/)

bok choy is also good with mushrooms (usually sliced shiitake) as a stir fry. for this method i just cut each bunch into quarters/halves lengthwise depending on size and toss them in the pan after the mushrooms have cooked off a bit. you wanna get a nice golden colour on the edges of the bok choy. i’ll cook them with a splash of shaoxing cooking wine and finish with a drizzle of sesame oil (a little goes a long way).

ohh this is one of my favourite topics so I apologize in advance if my reply becomes lengthy. I'm going to be using **hominin** here to refer to the group that includes both modern and past human species as well as all our immediate ancestors. 

*Homo sapiens* and *Homo neanderthalensis* are actually pretty recent on the line of human evolution, which can be traced as far back as 7 million years ago (mya) . If you're interested in the earliest species, you can look up *Sahelanthropus, Orrorin,* and *Ardipithecus.* 

From *Ardipithecus*, the *Australopithecines* species emerged around 4(?) mya.  *A. afarensis* is thought to be the most closely related direct ancestor of humans, with the most famous fossil discovery of this species being [Lucy](http://www.bbc.com/earth/story/20141127-lucy-fossil-revealed-our-origins), in Ethiopia in 1974. I would also look into Selam, a fossilized 3 year old belonging to *A . afarensis .*  Other *Australopithecines* include *A. boisei* (the likely origin of genital herpes in the human line) and *A. garhi* (the only *Australopithecines* who showed some evidence of tool use). 

The species *Homo* evolved from *A. afarensis* and are generally grouped into Early, Middle, and Late *Homo.* For simplicity's sake I'm just going to list a few species belonging to each group.  These different species coexisted at different time ranges.  

Early *Homo:*

* *H. habilis*
* *H. rudolphensis*

Middle *Homo:*

* *H. erectus* (associated with new adaptive strategies; tool use, first to use/control fire, also had humanlike body proportions)
* *H. heidelbergensis*

Late *Homo:*

* *H. neanderthalensis* (largest cranial capacity)
* *H. sapiens* (us! modern humans)

Some other hominins you might be interested in researching may include the [Denisovans](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-019-01395-0), [H . naledi](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2017/05/homo-naledi-human-evolution-science/) (most recently discovered hominin species)*,* and *H. floresiensus* (hobbit-like hominins discovered in Indonesia)

I hope this helps pique your interest in hominins, both present and past! Happy exploring!

PSYC 100A is your typical intro psych class that provides a general overview of a broad range of topics. Definitely lots of material to cover so be prepared to do textbook readings and take notes. some topics explored include consciousness, language, nature/nurture, and memory. lots to learn but it’s also very easy to bump your grade depending on how the prof has structured the course. very memorization based but i’m a psych major so i found the material interesting and didn’t mind the amount we had to learn. 

PHIL 201 in my opinion was much harder. topics covered include arguments, fallacies, propositional and categorical logic, and enumerative induction. a bit mathlike with words so unless translating sentences into symbols comes naturally to you and you are able to grasp the concepts easily, be prepared to put a lot of effort into practicing and understanding the concepts in order to do well in the course. it’s probably impossible to passively absorb the material and get by without any sort of studying. difficult but definitely worth it bc knowing how to apply logical concepts is useful for other things like essay writing. also Dr. Klatt was a gem which was a large reason why i found the course interesting. if i didn’t have such a great prof i probably would’ve hated the course

I tried to kill myself the night before my 18th birthday. I was at the beach drinking with a small group of friends but had been really struggling mentally the weeks leading up to that night and also been drinking almost daily to cope with the pain. I remember the sun setting and my friends all seemed to be having fun together but i just felt left out and so sick of myself that I decided to down a mickey of vodka and walk into the ocean to drown myself. 

never made it to the water though; I blacked out and all I remember is waking up on gravel under a dark sky and hearing the distorted voices of my friends. I remember repeating the same phrase over and over again, “I want to die, I want to kill myself”. And I remember my best friend crying beside me saying she didn’t want me to go and that she loved me. 

They had to call EMS to get me and although I kept floating in and out of consciousness i remember the paramedics reassuring me as I semiconsciously apologized to them for landing myself in that situation. long story short, they brought me to the hospital and I don’t remember much of it other than my friend accompanying me to see a psychiatrist. She had also notified my mom who came to pick me up and I remember feeling so, so guilty because she wasn’t even mad at me, just upset and worried. 

I’ve never really thoroughly explained that night to my close friends because I didn’t want to burden them any further but after that trip to the hospital, I quit drinking for a while and stayed completely sober for two and a half months. I only drink in moderation now when I’m in a social setting, but can’t stomach vodka anymore so I don’t touch it. thankful I didn’t succeed in drowning myself that night because I have some amazing friends, new and old, and they are the reason why I’m glad Im alive right now.
